basics.name: Michael Roberts
basics.label: Cybersecurity Student
basics.summary: Forward thinker bringing seven years of experience in information technology, handling and distributing classified material, and resolving complex technical issues. Proven ability to take initiative, support team objectives, and contribute to mission success. Excited to apply my skills and grow with a solution-oriented team. Open to relocation and completing the remainder of my degree program online for out-of-state opportunities.

highlights: Conducted vulnerability assessments using Nessus, configuring and scanning Metasploitable 2 to detect CVE-listed vulnerabilities and weaknesses. Researched and documented mitigation strategies such as system patching, disabling unused ports, and implementing firewall rules.
Completed NIST DoD RMF course, increased understanding of Risk Management Framework Security Controls and their application to IA.

Developed a Python script to scan system files for specific keywords and patterns using the os and regex libraries, incorporating loops, conditionals, and user-defined functions to generate a detailed report of the findings.
Setup Google Authenticator on Ubuntu server, enabling time-based authentication tokens and configuring SSH and PAM settings to require MFA.

Configured Splunk solution on Ubuntu to monitor security events, integrated system logs into data inputs, created search queries to track SSH failed login attempts, built a dashboard with a time chart panel, and simulated failed login attempts to validate the dashboard’s functionality.
Led 10-member team in maintaining 24/7 SATCOM data link supporting 120+ users, delivering 99.8% uptime for mission-critical systems essential to operational success.
Deployed iDirect GATR 950/1050 TS modems, Cisco ISR routers, and KG-250X encryptors, establishing a secure, segmented network for classified communications.
Designed on-the-spot redundant high-frequency (HF) communication to mitigate VoIP disruptions, ensuring uninterrupted reach-back for customers.
Developed documentation, records, and troubleshooting guides for Harris PRC-117G/152A/150C radios, lowering diagnostic time by 25%, minimizing repeat issues and accelerating hardware setup.
Enforced AES-256 and Type 1 encryption protocols, utilizing KVL 4000 and AN/PYQ-10 key loaders, ensuring compliance with DoD security protocols.
Led multi-agency emergency network project, configuring 391 APX6000/7500 radios to unify communication across 14 partners, reducing response times by 30% during crisis scenarios.

Diagnosed and resolved VSWR test failures, using signal generator and spectrum analyzer on 6 Mystic Star antennas, isolating faulty connectors and replacing damaged transmission lines to restore signal integrity for data links.
Restored 24/7 emergency alert functionality, repairing circuit overloads and replacing voltage regulator of mass notification system, brought node online within 30 minutes of reported outage.
